task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0414-service-catalog-safety-net.md exactly: (1) extend test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex with a new public function sweep_service_catalog_orphans/1, reusing the module's existing pg_stat_activity-based concurrent-invocation guard (current_application_name/1, concurrent_invocation_present?/2) rather than duplicating it; (2) wire it into test/test_helper.exs at the same two boundary points (before ExUnit.start(), inside the existing ExUnit.after_suite/1 callback) the existing tenant-schema sweep already uses; (3) no age threshold, per the design's own confirmed finding that no service_catalog row is ever legitimately held open across a test-process boundary; (4) on finding any row, warn-log every service_id/scope pair found, then delete unconditionally; (5) add the test coverage the design specifies (test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs, new file); (6) add the docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md note the design specifies.
acceptance_criteria: sweep_service_catalog_orphans/1 exists on Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper with the design's exact @spec, reusing current_application_name/1 and concurrent_invocation_present?/2 verbatim (no duplicated pg_stat_activity logic)
No age-threshold parameter added -- any row found at a boundary is treated as an anomaly unconditionally
On a nonzero find: a single :warning log naming every service_id/scope pair, then an unconditional DELETE (no WHERE clause, no scope filtering)
On a concurrent, non-sibling invocation: defers entirely (no read, no delete), returns {:deferred, :concurrent_invocation}
Never raises to test_helper.exs -- an outer failure is caught and reported as {:ok, %{deleted: 0}}
test/test_helper.exs calls the new function at both existing sweep_orphans/0 call sites (pre-ExUnit.start(), inside the same after_suite callback), not a second ExUnit.after_suite/1 registration

New test file test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs covers: empty table, mixed-scope leftover rows deleted unconditionally, concurrent-invocation deferral (rows survive), same-TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP sibling proceeds, and the never-raises failure-mode contract
docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md documents that service_catalog has no tenant-schema cleanup fallback and that the reaper is a crash safety net, not a substitute for per-test on_exit/1 cleanup

result.summary:
Implemented exactly per the approved design; no deviation, no scope creep, no lib/letflow/ file touched.

1) test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex: added a new moduledoc section ("ISS-0414") documenting the second responsibility, and a new public function sweep_service_catalog_orphans/1 (default arg Letflow.Repo) immediately before the module's private helpers. Algorithm matches design §2.4 exactly: Sandbox.mode(repo, :auto) -> compute own_tag via the existing private current_application_name/1 -> call the existing private concurrent_invocation_present?/2 -> if true, log :info and return {:deferred, :concurrent_invocation} without touching the table; if false, SELECT service_id, scope FROM service_catalog first, then on empty return {:ok, %{deleted: 0}} with no extra logging, on nonzero log a single :warning naming every "service_id (scope=...)" pair found and run an unconditional DELETE FROM service_catalog (no WHERE clause), returning {:ok, %{deleted: n}}. Outer rescue catches any exception, logs :error, returns {:ok, %{deleted: 0}}; after block restores Sandbox.mode(repo, :manual) unconditionally, matching sweep_orphans/2's own contract. Both concurrency-check private helpers are called, not duplicated -- confirmed by grep, zero new pg_stat_activity string literals outside the two existing ones.

2) test/test_helper.exs: added a new line calling Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_service_catalog_orphans(Letflow.Repo) immediately after the existing sweep_orphans() call, before ExUnit.start(...), with a short ISS-0414-attributing comment pointing at the design doc and the module's own moduledoc. Converted the existing single-line ExUnit.after_suite(fn _stats -> Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans() end) into a multi-statement anonymous function that also calls sweep_service_catalog_orphans(Letflow.Repo) -- one ExUnit.after_suite/1 registration, not two, per design §3.

3) test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs (new file): Letflow.DataCase, async: false, Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) in setup/on_exit, mirroring tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs's own pattern. Five test cases: (a) empty table -> {:ok, %{deleted: 0}}, table still empty; (b) hand-inserted scope: :global AND scope: :tenant rows (via Entry.insert_changeset/2, following service_catalog_test.exs's own fixture style) both deleted unconditionally, proving no scope-based filtering; (c) a real second Postgrex connection tagged as a distinct letflow_mixtest_* application_name (same technique tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs already uses for ISS-0110) -> {:deferred, :concurrent_invocation}, row survives untouched, then reclaimed once that connection closes; (d) a sibling connection sharing this invocation's own _grp<id> suffix (when this run actually carries one, i.e. under scripts/test_parallel.sh) proceeds rather than deferring (ISS-0217 exclusion, reused); when this invocation carries no group of its own, the test instead confirms the group-less-invocation behavior is unchanged (still defers against any other tag) rather than asserting a false sibling premise -- both branches exercise the identical reused concurrent_invocation_present?/2 logic, not a copy; (e) a BrokenRepo module (delegates get_dynamic_repo/0 to the real Letflow.Repo so Sandbox.mode/2 itself still succeeds, but whose query!/1 and query!/2 always raise) forces the SELECT-path failure and confirms {:ok, %{deleted: 0}} is returned, never an exception.

4) docs/guides/test_developer_guide.md: added a 5th bullet under section 1's "Additional principles" stating service_catalog has no tenant-schema cleanup fallback, that every test file writing to it must still clean up its own rows in on_exit/1 (citing service_catalog_test.exs's cleanup_entry!/1), and that the new suite-boundary reaper is a crash safety net, not a substitute -- any row it finds is itself logged as an anomaly.

VERIFICATION (all run for real, in the foreground, output quoted below -- not claimed):

- `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, 'Compiling 1 file (.ex)', exit 0.
- `mix format --check-formatted`: clean, exit 0.
- `mix test test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs --seed 0`: 'Result: 5 passed' (after two iteration fixes described below).
- `mix test test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs --seed 0`: 'Result: 39 passed' -- confirms no regression to the existing ISS-0064 reaper coverage or the ISS-0409-hardened REQ-191/REQ-192 suite.
- `mix test test/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator_test.exs test/letflow/routers/admin_services_test.exs --seed 0`: 'Result: 30 passed' -- the other two files that touch Letflow.ServiceCatalog, unaffected.
- A full `mix test` run was attempted twice per the task's optional final-check allowance but both exceeded the 600s foreground timeout and were moved to background by the tool; per this project's own core-directive against relying on a cross-turn background-task notification for a verification claim, both were killed (kill -9) rather than waited on, and this handoff's PASS is based entirely on the five foreground, synchronous, targeted runs quoted above. TEST-RUNNER should still run the authoritative full suite.

Two bugs were found and fixed while writing the new test file's own iteration, both confirmed by rerunning: (a) the failure-mode-contract test originally passed a bare stub module with no get_dynamic_repo/0 -- Sandbox.mode(repo, :auto)'s OWN failure inside the try body was correctly rescued, but the `after` block's Sandbox.mode(repo, :manual) call raised the identical exception a second time, uncaught by the try/rescue (which does not wrap its own `after`), crashing the test process -- this is a real, pre-existing structural property of the try/rescue/after shape shared with sweep_orphans/2's own contract, not a defect introduced here, but it means a repo argument must at minimum support Sandbox's own dynamic-repo lookup to safely exercise this contract; fixed by having the test's BrokenRepo delegate get_dynamic_repo/0 to the real Letflow.Repo and only fail on query!/1 and query!/2, isolating the forced failure to the realistic SELECT/DELETE path. (b) the sibling-guard test initially raced -- the second Postgrex connection's application_name was not yet guaranteed visible in pg_stat_activity when the sweep's own query ran; fixed by adding the same sanity SELECT 1 FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name = $1 check tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs's own ISS-0110 test already uses before asserting on the sweep's result.

Self-review checklist: no lib/letflow/process_instance.ex change (property test unaffected); no migration added (nothing to check for additive/reversible); no lib/letflow/ file touched at all, so no README.md state-diagram update applies. mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both run and clean.
result.routing: Route to Step 3 SECURITY-REVIEWER: although no lib/letflow/ file changed and no production route/migration is touched, this change adds test-support code that runs an unconditional, unfiltered DELETE FROM service_catalog against a REAL Postgres table (only ever the letflow_test* database per test/test_helper.exs's MIX_ENV=test guarantee, design doc §2.3) at every mix test invocation's suite boundary. Per this run's own instructions this is treated as a tenant-data-path change and routed through SECURITY-REVIEWER as a hard gate before REVIEWER, even though the table itself is global (no tenant_id/prefix) and the mechanism is structurally confined to the test database. SECURITY-REVIEWER should specifically confirm: (1) the dev/prod-unreachability argument (test/test_helper.exs is only ever loaded under `mix test`, which mix itself hardcodes to MIX_ENV=test before loading any config) actually holds and isn't circumventable by any invocation shape in this repo; (2) the unconditional, no-WHERE-clause DELETE is safe given the design's own confirmed finding (§0's setup_all/seed-script greps) that no legitimate non-test row can ever appear in this table at a suite boundary; (3) the BrokenRepo test fixture in test/support/service_catalog_reaper_test.exs introduces no risk of ever running against a real repo by accident.
